source_text: So, in cases where "Lean reports no owning module" can we not just read the source code?

fragments.text: So, in cases where "Lean reports no owning module" can we not just read the source code?

reply_text:
㊥ Yes. The probe asks Lean which module owns a constant name, and `Lean.__instance_4563` is the port's own synthetic name for an anonymous instance, so Lean has never heard of it. But the port's declaration record already holds its source file and line, `Init/Notation.lean:105`, and the module follows from the path. So the probe can take a source location instead of a name. I've sent that to codex-30, who was idle.

㊯ (codex-30, `invoke-1791238923646-33195`) The probe gets a second way in: a declaration by source path and line. It derives the owning module from the path (`Init/Notation.lean` → `Init.Notation`), then runs the same cold production compile of that one declaration with its dependencies. The compile path doesn't change. The check is to compile `Init/Notation.lean:105` this way, and compare its time with a full `mkListNode` cold run.

🈳 (side question in the packet) Lean gives that instance a generated `inst…` name, not `__instance_4563`. codex-30 will find Lean's actual name, and check whether the port's `__instance_N` names ever appear in a compared term. If they do, matching Lean's instance names becomes its own packet.

㊟ (why it matters) If compiling one declaration takes a minute or two instead of 14, every lane can reproduce its stop that way. Combined with the real-path rule, that removes most of the waiting.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(codex-31, `invoke-1791238019292-33177`: faster cold path, measurement only) Three questions, answered in `coldspeed.md`, before anything is built:
1. **Where does a cold run's time go?** Per-declaration timings on `epsilonInfo` and `mkListNode`.
2. **Would a baseline help?** Does the cache key make any compiler change invalidate every declaration? If so, a stored cold baseline buys nothing.
3. **Is reuse equivalent?** Does a run from a copied cold baseline, with nothing changed, produce byte-identical generated code and the same comparator results on 3 rows?
